title: Communicate to Play: Pragmatic Reasoning for Efficient Cross-Cultural Communication in Codenames
findings: Training word embeddings on data from specific religious groups (Catholic vs. non-Catholic) improves a model's ability to guess words in Codenames in a way that aligns with those groups. This indicates the models learn group-specific common ground, with a notable performance difference (10.99%) when a model trained on one religious group's data is tested on the other's, highlighting distinct cultural patterns in gameplay.
